description: a when handler delivered by the HOST, through the tick dispatcher, is charged exactly like one fired synchronously at registration. when has two delivery paths - the direct invokeWhenHandler call executeWhenStatement makes for the immediate "start" fire, and the tick drain for host-delivered named events - and when-firing-counts-against-budget only exercises the first, so charging one but not the other passed the whole corpus. The empty body makes the firing the only chargeable thing: the registration, the wait statement, and the first of its now-charged ticks consume the budget of 3, so the handler's own firing is the instruction that cannot be afforded and raises ol-limit. An implementation that charged only the registration-time path completes this program cleanly. The budget was 2 before issue #953 made each wait tick a charged instruction; it was re-derived to 3 so the run folds to the byte-identical event stream and refuses the same firing, at the same source span
